clue.text: Photographers follow Pope with shouted nickname?

parts.note: the Pope is Papa, father of the Church

indicators.note: said out loud, so the nickname's sound is what counts, not its spelling

parts.note: Ratzi was a nickname for Pope Benedict XVI, born Joseph Ratzinger

explanation.surface: Press photographers trail the Pope, yelling a teasing nickname at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shouted' says the sound of RATZI is entered as RAZZI. Pope Benedict XVI was nicknamed 'Papa Ratzi', which says the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paparazzi are freelance press cameramen who chase celebrities for candid shots.

clue.text: It may contain cartridge, modified silencer and instrument inside that makes lead go further

parts.note: a fountain pen may hold an ink cartridge

indicators.note: the musical instrument is placed within the rearranged letters
altered, so the letters of silencer are rearranged

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A gun with a cartridge and a modified silencer that makes lead travel further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' and 'inside' are the signals; cartridge, silencer and lead all suggest a gun, but the lead here is the graphite core of a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpening gadget shaves the wooden casing so more of the graphite core can be used.

clue.text: Road enjoyed by pedestrian probably is

definitions.text: Road enjoyed by pedestrian probably is

parts.words: Road enjoyed by pedestrian probably is
parts.note: describes the surface a walker would welcome under foot on a road

explanation.definitionFit: A paved road has a hard smooth surface of slabs or asphalt, pleasant to walk on.

clue.text: Upset, learnt sax as means of unwinding

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters of learnt and sax are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated by learning the saxophone, which was meant to relax them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges LEARNT and SAX. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxants are drugs or remedies that ease tension in the body.

clue.text: Dedicated heads of Arab League observers enter Egyptian region after uprising …

indicators.note: the initials go into the turned region name
in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Suez is the canal region of Egypt

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Keen Arab League monitors arrive in an Egyptian area after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after uprising' turns SUEZ into ZEUS, and 'enter' puts A, L, O into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous means devoted and fervent in pursuit of a cause.

clue.text: … coming from neighbouring country, infiltrating while arsing around

indicators.note: turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
sneaking inside the words while arsing, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Following on from the Egyptian clue, a neighbour's agent sneaks in while fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' picks ILEARSI out of 'while arsing' and 'around' turns it backwards. The ellipsis links this clue to the Egyptian one above, which is why the definition can say neighbouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel borders Egypt, so something native to it comes from a neighbouring land.

clue.text: Striker's game

definitions.meaning: something struck to make a flame
a sporting contest between two sides

explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck to light it, and a match is also a fixture played between teams.

clue.text: Chap to hoard one's Euros

indicators.note: to keep stored away, so the title holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man
one is I, so one's is I'S
E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: A man stashing away all his euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hoard' is the container signal, and the whole clue doubles as a description of a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person who saves money obsessively and spends as little as possible.

clue.text: Street cut off, Oval Station in chaos-it's not helping

indicators.note: thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
removed from the word station, so its opening letters go

explanation.surface: A street closed, and the Oval Underground station in turmoil, which doesn't help commuters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' removes ST from Station to leave ATION, and 'in chaos' rearranges OVAL with it. The Oval is a London cricket ground with a Tube station.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any effect or use, so achieving nothing helpful.

clue.text: Content of hot download on phone? Space agency, perhaps, turning up alien body

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a phone download is an app

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read upwards, so both are turned

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency
say is used for for example or perhaps

indicators.note: strange, so the letters of body are rearranged

explanation.surface: Downloading a phone app about space aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns NASA SAY into YASASAN, and 'alien' rearranges BODY into DBOY. The phrase is a British idiom for perfectly contented.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile means utterly carefree and cheerful, an idiom for being pleased.

clue.text: Back introduction of voice over in director's story

indicators.note: read backwards, so the whole built-up word is turned round at the end
the voice and over letters go inside the film-maker's name

parts.note: Woody Allen is a famous film director

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word voice

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A film-maker's story gets a voice-over added at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: V and O go inside ALLEN to give ALLEVON, and 'Back' turns that whole word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a piece of prose fiction.

clue.text: Reared pure, riddled with sin?

indicators.note: the letters of pure are shot through with those of sin and jumbled together

explanation.surface: Something reared as pure turns out to be full of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddled with' mixes PURE with SIN to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose up and reared both describe standing up on hind legs or in revolt.

clue.text: It points to catalogue

definitions.meaning: an ordered list of references, as at the back of a book

explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the pointing digit, and an index is also a listing of topics in a book.

clue.text: 0-5 year-end thrashing — get prepared to be roasted!

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: a beating that knocks the letters of year-end about

parts.note: the letters of this word taken as they stand

explanation.surface: A team losing 0-5 at the end of the season is ready for a roasting from the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashing' is the anagram signal, playing on a heavy football defeat; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-ready food is sold already trimmed and dressed so it can go straight in to cook.

clue.text: Dissipate with abandon as not old and wise

definitions.text: Dissipate with abandon as not old and wise

parts.words: Dissipate with abandon as not old and wise
parts.note: a description of reckless youthful excess, indulged in by those still young and foolish

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to indulge in wild behaviour while young, before settling down.

clue.text: By turns, was tearful and blown away

parts.note: winds, as a road or a key turns
wept means cried

explanation.surface: Someone alternately crying and being blown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept describes something exposed to and swept by strong gusts.

clue.text: Live cushioned by something false, a kind of security

indicators.note: padded on both sides, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Living with false teeth cushioned in, feeling secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cushioned by' is the container signal: false teeth sit on a cushion of gum.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a bond issued by a company, a loan backed by its assets.

clue.text: Northern Irish labour's in unsettled period when things are going badly

definitions.text: period when things are going badly

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Northern Irish workers are in a troubled period of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges N, IRISH, LABOURS and IN. The Latin phrase became famous when Queen Elizabeth II used it of 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a horrible year, a phrase for a twelvemonth full of misfortunes.

clue.text: Work on bone problem in American animal

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Operating on a bone problem in an American creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opossum is a marsupial native to the Americas.

clue.text: Right weary, with a bit of hesitation about it, he goes to bed

indicators.note: the hesitation sound wraps around the word for weary

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: Feeling tired and hesitating a little before heading to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it' is the container signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who withdraws for the night, since to retire is to go to bed.

clue.text: Be cautious with evidence of infected toenail?

definitions.meaning: to tread warily and avoid committing oneself
a foot oozing pus, read literally

explanation.surface: Treading warily because of a nasty infected toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act timidly; read literally, a pus-filled foot shows infection.

clue.text: Cries out one of two possible answers after accepting "50-50"

indicators.note: taking in, so the fifties go inside the reply

parts.note: yes, the alternative to no
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant shouts an answer after taking the fifty-fifty lifeline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after accepting' is the container signal. The fifty-fifty lifeline, which leaves two possible answers, is from the quiz show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Yells are loud shouts or cries.

clue.text: Stocking sterling in place of Swiss Francs?

indicators.note: the money sign goes inside the name of the Swiss town

parts.note: Nyon is a town in Switzerland, where Swiss francs are spent
L is the symbol for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Swapping pounds for Swiss francs to buy hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: Nyon is a town on Lake Geneva; 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are stockings made from the synthetic fibre, so the fibre stands for the stocking.

clue.text: Climber using a spike on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, read upwards, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A mountaineer using a spike while ascending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns A NAIL backwards. 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs up trees in tropical forests.

clue.text: Not having point, after final point's deducted-but they do have points

indicators.note: the last compass point, south, comes off the end of the word

parts.note: pointless, without purpose, meaning needless

explanation.surface: A pointless remark loses its last point, yet sharp things have points.
explanation.walkthrough: S is south, a compass point; 'after final point's deducted' drops the last S of NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing pins and similar sharp tools each end in a sharp tip.

clue.text: Expressed regret at wounding comment a word not meant to be understood

definitions.text: a word not meant to be understood

indicators.note: spoken, so the word for regret counts only by its sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: Someone said sorry for a hurtful remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressed' turns RUE into its sound-alike RHU. Actors murmur the word over and over to make background crowd noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish muttered by stage extras to imitate indistinct conversation, meant only as noise.

clue.text: Was consumer taken in by rights estimates?

indicators.note: held inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: R stands for right, so two of them are R's
someone who consumed food ate

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether consumer-rights figures fooled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts ATE between the two R's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates are assessments or valuations, as when one rates a chance or a cost.

clue.text: My career revolves around money, essentially

definitions.text: My career revolves around money, essentially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the central letter
turns round, so the letters of my career are spun into a new order
at its essence or heart, the middle letter of the word money

explanation.surface: Someone admits their whole working life is about cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolves' rearranges MYCAREER around N, the centre of money that 'essentially' picks out, and the whole clue describes a hired soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier for hire, or anyone motivated chiefly by payment, has a working life centred on cash.
